mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry or corporate registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where the issuing state is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official extract from the shareholders' register / UBO register identifying all Individuals with Significant Control over each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office, corporate secretary, or competent corporate registry of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport or national identity card for each ultimate beneficial owner and proposed director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Commissioner of Oaths in the country of document issue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague-party jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank branch in the beneficial owner's or corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the designated competent authority in the issuing jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, shareholders, and Individuals with Significant Control against FINTRAC foreign and domestic Politically Exposed Persons categories; Canadian sanctions lists enforced under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; the UN Security Council Consolidated List; the OFAC SDN List where USD settlement via US correspondent banks is anticipated; and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Canada's Sergei Magnitsky Law). Screening must be completed before onboarding and updated periodically, with risk-based enhanced measures for non-face-to-face corporate clients and medium-risk re-invoicing trade activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) — https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A CBCA name may be in English, French, or a combined bilingual form. Names must be expressible in the Latin alphabet using English/French words or transliterations of foreign-language names; a French legal element is permitted. The corporate name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive/geographic element, and a legal element such as 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', 'Limitée', 'Incorporée', or abbreviations 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée', or 'Inc.'. The name must not be confusingly similar to existing federal/provincial names, reserved names, or registered trademarks, and must not contain obscene or objectionable matter or imply a connection with the Crown or a government institution.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director refuses an available-name request, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director under the CBCA within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the original NUANS report, a revised proposed name, and any consent or release letters from conflicting name holders or trademark owners. If the refusal is maintained, judicial review may be brought in the Federal Court within 30 days under s. 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act. A name reservation may be renewed by submitting a renewal request before expiry; if no renewal is filed, a fresh NUANS search and new filing will be required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. A virtual office with a real Canadian street address and daytime service-of-process capability can satisfy the CBCA registered-office provision, but it will not create commercial substance for re-invoicing operations. Banks, trade finance counterparties, CRA and FINTRAC will generally expect some degree of physical operational activity, Canadian records, resident personnel, or substantive management presence in Canada for medium-risk enhanced AML treatment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: 10-15% annual probability of CRA or police verification in the ordinary course; elevated to 25-40% if the company applies for trade finance, uses virtual office only, processes large invoice volumes, or experiences adverse regulatory triggers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, Corporations Canada fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official legalization tariffs plus market shipping/courier charges.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 8, 19, 100-101, 106, 114, 128, 163
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed through the Corporations Canada online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA. The corporation may issue one or more shares with no par value; no escrow account or paid-up capital undertaking is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the board of directors hereby: 1. Accepts the subscription for common shares set forth in the Articles of Incorporation and authorizes issuance to the subscriber upon receipt of agreed consideration; 2. Adopts the registered office at the address stated in the Articles and appoints the named individual as registered agent; 3. Appoints the following officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until resignation or successor election; 4. Approves opening corporate bank accounts and authorizes designated officers to execute banking resolutions; 5. Ratifies all actions taken by the sole incorporator and directs completion of any required post-incorporation returns and filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada - NUANS Name Search through accredited providers or the Corporations Canada online name request service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name for NUANS pre-clearance. Ensure the name is distinctive and does not conflict with existing corporate names or trademarks. Retain the NUANS report for attachment to the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, revise the name or add a distinctive element and re-run the NUANS search. Alternatively, proceed with a numbered company name under the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada - Corporate Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 online, entering the corporate name (or numbered corporation designation), registered office address, share structure, restrictions on share transfers, and the number of directors. Select the province or territory of the registered office. Pay the filing fee by credit card and submit electronically. Electronic submission produces a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form 4003 Consent to Act as Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, review the deficiency notice in the online portal, correct the required fields, and resubmit within the stated deadline. If rejected, re-file with corrected information and pay a new filing fee if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada and the applicable provincial registry for extra-provincial registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office is located in the province selected in the Articles. If applicable, appoint an individual or corporation authorized to carry on business in that province as the registered agent. Where a change occurs after incorporation, file Form 4006 Notice of Change of Registered Office and Registered Agent.
required_dossiers: Written consent of the registered agent, if applicable
Form 4006 if changing office after incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is invalid because it is a post office box or outside the jurisdiction, file a corrected Notice of Change of Registered Office and Agent. Verify acceptance with the corporations registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting. The board shall accept the share subscription, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, approve bylaws, set the financial year-end, and approve the banking resolution. Issue share certificates after subscription funds are received.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board lacks quorum, reschedule the meeting or obtain signed written consent. If the share subscription is defective, pass a corrective board resolution and amend the share register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Initial Return with Corporations Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada - Initial Return Online Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 months after incorporation, file the Initial Return online or in paper form. Provide the registered office address, the list of directors, and any prescribed information. Verify that all officer and director details are correct before submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is rejected, correct the missing or inconsistent data and resubmit. If the corporation is dissolved for failure to file, apply for revival under the CBCA after curing the default.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate Business Number and Corporate Bank Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online and a Canadian chartered bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and the first board resolution, open a corporate bank account. Register the corporation for the CRA business number through Business Registration Online and activate income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts as applicable. For a re-invoicing trade entity, confirm whether an import/export account is needed for physical goods movement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA account activation is delayed, contact the CRA Business Enquiries line to confirm the business number. For banking problems, provide an updated resolution or supplementary identification to the bank's compliance officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No federal industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 4690 re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation; municipal business licensing under the applicable provincial Business Licence Act may apply if an office or warehouse is physically established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operating, manufacturing, or trade intermediary permit is required under federal law for general re-invoicing operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (federal lead); provincial and municipal environmental authorities may apply if a physical facility is established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based commercial re-invoicing activity does not trigger a federal environmental impact assessment under the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or waste discharge thresholds apply to a pure re-invoicing hub. If the entity later engages in warehousing or repackaging, compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act release notices and applicable provincial wastewater and solid waste standards will be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Workplace safety compliance under the Canada Labour Code, Part II and the National Fire Code. For any leased office or warehouse space, obtain a building occupancy certificate, fire safety inspection clearance, and first aid assessment from the local fire marshal and occupational health and safety authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – federal GST/HST and corporate income tax administration; official portal: www.canada.ca/revenue-agency; business portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account (MyBA), GST/HST NETFILE; customs/export filing administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) via the Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not resident in Canada that carries on commercial activity in Canada (including a re-invoicing/trading hub) applies for a CRA Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST program account using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) or, if no Canadian presence, Form RC1A (Request for a Business Number for Non-Residents), submitted by mail or fax to the Sudbury Tax Centre, accompanied by the foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, resolutions designating a Canadian agent/contact, and, where relevant, a power of attorney (Form T1013). Alternatively, Canadian-based entities may register online via the Government of Canada Business Registration Online service. The CRA assigns a 9-digit BN with a program account suffix (e.g., RT for GST/HST, RC for income tax) and issues a confirmation of registration; GST/HST registration is backdated to the date the CAD 30,000 threshold was exceeded. Exporters should also obtain a CBSA exporter business number linked to the BN where goods will be declared under the Customs Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; a federal/provincial Business Corporation is a taxable Canadian corporation (ITA s. 89(1)) taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Relevant elections for cross-border trade include the ETA s. 273 GST/HST grouping election (closely related group members filing as a single registrant; forms GST25/GST26), the ETA small-supplier voluntary registration election, and, for non-residents, the ITA ss. 216 and 219 elective returns. For hybrid mismatch outcomes, Canada's anti-hybrid rules (ITA ss. 18.4 and 18.5, addressing reverse hybrids and deduction/non-inclusion mismatches) operate alongside CRA entity classification determinations; where a foreign transparent entity is interposed, a dedicated CRA technical ruling should be obtained before structuring.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the Canadian Dollar (CAD). No exchange control is exercised under the Currency Act or the Bank of Canada Act. Profit remittances, dividends, royalties, and trade payments to non-residents are unrestricted, subject to anti-money laundering (PCMLTFA) record keeping and associated reporting. No prior approval is required for capital inflows or outflows; however, transactions must be reported under the Canadian Payments Act and, for certain cross-border transfers, to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency or converted freely. Invoices and bank references must record a standard Canadian export declaration (via Statistics Canada / Canadian Border Services Agency) for trade statistics, but no repatriation or liquidation timeline applies. For re-invoicing intermediaries, the tax authority (CRA) will require transfer pricing documentation to support intercompany settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and FX Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium (restricted). Canada does not license pure-play electronic money institutions; a fintech wishing to open accounts for a re-invoicing entity must either hold a bank license, an MSB/MT registration with FINTRAC, or operate as a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). Foreign EMIs without Canadian presence have limited or no standalone viability; they may rely on white-label sponsorship by a Schedule I bank. Enhanced due diligence and PCMLTFA compliance are mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For most Canadian Schedule I banks, directors of a non-resident corporation must appear in person or by notarized corporate authorization; pure remote opening is generally not permitted for businesses with medium-risk re-invoicing profiles unless the bank has a licensed e-KYC flow. A mandatory video interview with the compliance officer is standard. Directors may appoint a corporate signing officer (resident agent) with Power of Attorney, but ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must be disclosed and verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained discrepancy between declared business activity and transaction profile (large round sum flows, rapid in-out)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts and purchase orders; vendor and customer onboarding files; independent credit/corporate registry excerpt; 12-month projected and historical transaction statements; organizational chart and UBO trust deed; tax invoice and shipping logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership or control residing in low-tax jurisdiction without substantive presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA/GAAR-compliant transfer pricing study; business purpose memorandum; board resolutions authorizing re-invoicing hub; entity registries, register of directors/UBO; operational substance evidence (office lease, payroll, local management).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large number of cross-border wires to or from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions/PEP screening results; FATF guideline compliance; source-of-funds and purpose-of-payment checklist; correspondent bank codes and end-beneficiary verification; trade documents (bills of lading, packing lists, inspection certificates).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of audited financial statements or low capitalization for an intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date financial statements (audited or review engagement); shareholder capital confirmation; bank reference letters; CRS/FATCA classification; pre-approval of financial covenants with the relationship manager.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: inbound equity injections from a parent entity must be transmitted via SWIFT wire using standard purpose code for foreign direct investment (e.g., balance-of-payments code 1000 'Capital contribution' or CFP code). The receiving Canadian Schedule I bank will require supporting board resolution, subscription agreement, and a capital identity memorandum. FINTRAC EFT thresholds: report any electronic fund transfer of CAD 10,000 or more. The entity must file the appropriate CRA schedule for paid-up capital; no pre-clearance is required under the Investment Canada Act unless the investor is a non-Canadian controlling acquisition above threshold (for re-invoicing hub, routine operating capital usually exempt).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 single or serial payments with proper remittance information (e.g., ISPA/ISO 20022 fields); commercial letters of credit (LC) opened via Canadian trade finance desks with MT700, amendments MT707, and presentation under UCP600. Disbursements for intercompany re-invoicing must be supported by intercompany purchase agreements, tax invoices, and completed T106 (or CRA cross-sections) reporting. Use of CLS Bank netting for FX payments is not applicable to CAD commodity trade; instead, rely on correspondent bank clearing through Canadian Dollar Bulk Electronic Payment System (CAD-BEPS) / Payments Canada (formerly ACSS, now Lynx for SWIFT-capable values).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards (maturity <= 12 months) for CAD/USD and other liquid trade currencies, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or long-form FX confirmation
Over-the-counter (OTC) non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or restricted currencies where CAD convertibility is not achievable
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (for financing legacy) provided the hedging strategy mirrors a contracted trade or funding exposure
Plain vanilla FX swaps and single-currency floating-to-fixed interest rate swaps executable through Schedule I bank derivatives trading desks
Bank-offered FX vanilla options (calls and puts) on major trade currencies, subject to OSFI prudential limits and internal hedging policy approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) filed online via Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director, Corporations Canada; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 calendar days after the corporation's anniversary of incorporation (e.g., if incorporated on April 1, the annual return is due on May 31).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100 if submitted beyond the 60-day window; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212, after notice and 90-day cure period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including federal and provincial portions, schedules, and financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid balance, plus 1% per month for each full month up to 12 months; interest accrues on unpaid amounts; continued failure may lead to criminal prosecution and revocation of privileges; CRA may issue demand to file; administrative strike-off not applicable under CBCA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A CBCA federal corporation must appoint an independent auditor unless it is a non-distributing corporation and shareholders pass a unanimous resolution waiving the statutory audit. Decisioning thresholds are based on distributing status, not revenue or asset size; however, provincial securities laws and bank/lender covenants may require audit or review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for Canadian private corporations; annual financial statements must be prepared for shareholders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under CBCA, an annual review of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be carried out; any share transfer or change in significant control must be recorded within 15 days. No separate federal UBO filing is required; confirmation occurs inside corporate records, and the annual return to Corporations Canada confirms only registered office and director information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 500 per year for registered office and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 15,000 per engagement for a small-to-mid-size federal corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (9% federal) for CCPCs on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; provincial credits may apply; SR&ED tax credits for qualifying R&D (not typical for re-invoicing).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed via CRA's e-file or NETFILE (mandatory for most corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., Dec 31 year-end → June 30 deadline)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross sales, commissions, re-invoicing income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source and worldwide income if resident; for non-resident, report only Canadian-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses (cost of goods sold, operating expenses, interest, TP adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses reasonably allocated to Canadian-source income; maintain contemporaneous TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after loss carryovers and deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty provisions for business profits (Article 7) if applicable; ensure no permanent establishment triggers full taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable (15% of taxable income, less credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits if applicable; consider provincial allocation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax payable (varies by province; e.g., Ontario 11.5%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to provinces based on permanent establishment; file provincial schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed TP disclosures (Form T106) if transactions with non-residents exceed thresholds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File T106 if total value of transactions with non-arm's length non-residents exceeds CAD 1 million (goods) or CAD 50,000 (services, interest, royalties).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty up to 10%; interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (federal) on dividends paid to non-residents; reduced under tax treaties (e.g., 5% for substantial shareholding, 15% otherwise under US-Canada treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding, non-resident recipient must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR301) to the payer; payer must withhold at treaty rate if certificate is on file; otherwise, withhold at 25% and recipient may apply for refund via Form NR7.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 25%, royalties 25%; treaty rates: interest 0% (US, many treaties), royalties 10% (US, 0% for certain IP).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File required if gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million and transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 5 million (or if specifically requested by CRA).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires economic substance for treaty benefits; no separate ESR, but CRA may challenge transactions lacking commercial rationale.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or fraudulent re-invoicing to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239; fines up to 200% of tax evaded; imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes (s.160) and for negligence; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Re-invoicing entity with no real business activity, no employees, no office, or no decision-making in Canada; used solely to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may deny treaty benefits, reassess income, apply GAAR penalties (25% of tax benefit), and impose interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed for penalties if they knowingly participated in sham arrangements; potential criminal charges for conspiracy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business (MSB) if handling large wire transfers; failure to report suspicious transactions under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million per violation; criminal penalties up to CAD 2 million and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to CAD 500,000 and imprisoned if they knowingly fail to comply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices resulting in understated Canadian income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust prices, impose penalties up to 10% of the net adjustment (if gross negligence), plus interest; documentation penalties up to CAD 24,000 per failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they signed false or incomplete returns; potential criminal liability for tax evasion.
